summary: Validated the SEC-4 close-out (server-resolved paid-feature region gating extended from /duel and /duel/chips to /tournaments) end-to-end against the 5 ACs given in the task. All 5 pass. AC-2 (rendering mode / no paid markup in first HTML) verified live and independently: ran my own `pnpm build` in app/, parsed .next/prerender-manifest.json directly ('/tournaments' absent from both static routes and dynamicRoutes; 25 static routes total, none tournament-related), started `pnpm start` locally and curled http://localhost:3411/tournaments anonymously — response is Cache-Control: private/no-store (not shared-cacheable), body contains zero occurrences of 'Join queue', 'Choose entry fee', or tier-chip markup, and exactly one occurrence of the SignInGate copy 'Sign in to enter tournaments', confirming the known caveat (anonymous always shows SignInGate) without false-alarming on the negative claim AC-2 actually requires. AC-1 (blocked region never sees the tier picker/Join queue, including first frame) verified by code inspection since no live authenticated session is available in this environment: TournamentList.tsx's render is a single top-level ternary (!user -> SignInGate, !geoAllowed -> region block, else -> tier picker + Join queue) with no other path; `geoAllowed` is seeded via useState(serverAllowed) inside useRankedEligibility so the first client render already matches the server-resolved decision (no optimistic-true window); initialGeoAllowed is a required prop with no default, supplied only by app/app/tournaments/page.tsx, which resolves it server-side via resolveRankedEligibility(await headers()) — grepped the repo, exactly one caller of TournamentList. AC-3 (queue-route guard structural parity) verified by my own independent side-by-side read of queue/route.ts vs. checkout/route.ts vs. register/route.ts (not solely citing the three upstream agents): identical call, check, 403 GEO_BLOCKED envelope, and position (after requireAuth, before checkRateLimit) across all three; import depth (4 levels vs siblings' 5) is correct for queue/route.ts's shallower nesting. Added one piece of positive evidence none of the upstream agents' own handoffs framed this way: my own fresh `pnpm build` (run for AC-2) emitted `ƒ /api/tournaments/queue` in the route table, which is proof the import resolves via webpack independent of typecheck (the file is still @ts-nocheck, confirmed at line 1) and independent of trusting the prior three builds. AC-4 (no regression) verified live via git diff HEAD on paidDuelGeo.ts, rankedEligibility.ts, useRankedEligibility.ts, and both checkout/register route files — all five return 0 diff lines. AC-5 (coherent UX, queue-join flow otherwise unaffected) verified by reading the diff on TournamentList.tsx: the only changes are one import, the new required prop/interface, one hook call, and one new ternary branch inserted between the existing !user and else branches; handleJoin and the four-way joinState render (idle/joining/queued/error) are byte-identical to before. Also confirmed db/tournaments.ts (chip debit, bracket-fill) and config/tournaments.ts (kill switch) are byte-untouched. Independently re-ran all app-level gates myself after my own build/curl session (lint clean, typecheck clean, test 745/745 passing) and reverted the app/next-env.d.ts churn from my own pnpm build per the repo's recorded recurring pitfall, then re-confirmed typecheck clean. Final git status is exactly the intended 4-file diff (3 code files + loop/learnings.md) plus this stage's own report/handoff additions and the four untracked upstream handoff JSONs — no residue from my build/curl/kill-server session. One process note, not a blocking finding: loop/spec.md (the repo's paths.spec) currently documents an unrelated feature (mobile Quick Play), not this SEC-4 close-out, so there is no Flows/AC section in the formal spec file for this change to check against structurally. I validated against the AC-1..AC-5 given directly in this stage's task instead, consistent with how software-engineer/verifier/reviewer/security-reviewer all scoped this cycle (against the SEC-4 security finding and the already-reviewed /duel pattern, not loop/spec.md). Did not treat this as a structural spec-gate failure requiring loop-back, since no new user-facing flow was introduced (existing join-queue UX is unchanged, only a region gate was added) and three independent prior agents already treated this scope as authoritative without objection — but flagging the drift so it doesn't compound across future cycles.
goal: Validate AC-1 through AC-5 for the /tournaments region-gating SEC-4 close-out end-to-end, using live build/curl evidence where possible and explicit code-inspection evidence where a live authenticated session is unavailable, per the task's documented method and caveats.

structuralSpecGate.note: loop/spec.md (paths.spec) documents an unrelated feature (mobile Quick Play) and has no Flows/AC section for this SEC-4 change. Not treated as a blocking structural gate failure because no new user-facing flow was introduced by this diff and all four prior agents this cycle scoped their work against the SEC-4 security finding rather than loop/spec.md without objection. Flagged as a learning for the orchestrator/spec owner instead of looping back software-engineer, since there is no missing Flows/AC content to write for a change whose entire job is adding a server-side gate in front of an already-specified, already-shipped UI.

learnings.insight: loop/spec.md (this repo's paths.spec, the qa-acceptance role's default AC source) currently documents 'Mobile Quick Play', a completely unrelated feature, while four consecutive agents this cycle (software-engineer, verifier, reviewer, security-reviewer) correctly scoped their work against a security-reviewer-filed finding (SEC-4) and an existing shipped pattern instead. This worked fine for a narrow security-hardening change with no new user flow, but the drift means qa-acceptance's default instruction ('ACs live at paths.spec') was silently false for this entire cycle and had to be overridden by task-provided ACs.
learnings.action: When a cycle's goal is a security/tech-debt close-out rather than a new spec'd feature, either point qa-acceptance explicitly at the finding/ledger entry it should validate against (as this task did) or keep loop/spec.md as a rolling multi-goal doc so it does not silently point at a stale, unrelated feature. Do not let qa-acceptance's default 'read paths.spec' instruction go unchallenged when the task message already supplies the real ACs — but do surface the mismatch, as this handoff does, so it doesn't compound.

learnings.insight: For a @ts-nocheck'd route file, a fresh `pnpm build` run taken for an unrelated AC (here, AC-2's prerender-manifest check) doubles as independent, stronger evidence for a different AC (AC-3's import-resolution claim) than typecheck ever could — the route table entry `f /api/tournaments/queue` only appears if webpack successfully resolved every import in that file. This is cheaper than a dedicated build-just-for-this-import verification step.
learnings.action: When a diff includes both a rendering-mode claim (needs a build) and an edit inside a @ts-nocheck file (needs import-resolution proof beyond typecheck), run one build and extract both pieces of evidence from it rather than treating them as separate verification tasks.

learnings.insight: Fourth consecutive agent this cycle (software-engineer, verifier, reviewer, security-reviewer, now qa-acceptance) independently reproduced the prerender-manifest.json evidence via a fresh local build rather than trusting the prior three. All five reproductions agree. This is thorough but increasingly redundant CPU/time cost for a claim that has now been independently re-derived five times across one cycle with identical results each time.
learnings.action: Consider whether a single shared, timestamped build artifact (or a CI job that publishes the route table + prerender-manifest diff once per PR) could let downstream stages cite one canonical build rather than each re-running pnpm build. Not urgent — the redundancy has caught zero discrepancies across five independent runs this cycle — but it's the same underlying suggestion reviewer already made about adding pnpm build to CI.
